guard: every P7 kind reaches its per-space location through ONE migrating choke point, and the owners that must not migrate address the same layout it does
why: All five segmented kinds have an absent-means-MINT writer. That makes the read-fallback the
obvious-looking implementation - resolve the canonical location, fall back to the flat one -
into the worst one available: on a root whose material has not moved yet, the canonical read
answers ABSENT and the writer mints a SECOND live credential beside the one the running daemons
hold. Nothing errors. The split shows up later as a daemon the broker refuses, on a root where
both files look valid. So the property is not `the key is right`; it is `the move happened
before anyone could read absence`, which is why the migration lives inside the resolver rather
than beside it, and why the refusals must travel OUT through the resolver instead of being
caught there. The last mutation guards the other end: the hosted arm must not answer with the
pre-P7 flat kind, because a host provisions from the key this returns.

mutations.name: the resolver stops moving material and becomes a pure key builder (the read-fallback, shipped)
mutations.find:
if (!composition.injected) migrateLegacyCotalMaterial(composition.root, space, kind);
  return segmentedKey(kind, space);
mutations.replace:
if (!composition.injected && composition.root === "") migrateLegacyCotalMaterial(composition.root, space, kind);
  return segmentedKey(kind, space);
mutations.expectRed: delivery.creds: the FS arm MOVED the legacy copy on first touch
mutations.cell: the FS arm migrates on first touch, so no absent-means-mint writer ever reads absence past a flat copy

mutations.name: the fifth kind's wrapper composes the path itself instead of going through the choke point
mutations.expectRed: membership.json: the path wrapper migrates on first touch too
mutations.cell: the kind whose wrapper returns a PATH rather than a key is held to the same first-touch move

mutations.name: the wrapper catches the choke point's refusal, laundering an ambiguous root into a confident key
mutations.expectRed: rule 3 refuses through the named wrapper, not only through the choke point
mutations.cell: rules 3 and 4 reach the caller through the wrapper - a swallowed refusal is a silent second mint

mutations.name: the hosted arm answers with the bare kind, as a composition with no root to segment by would
mutations.expectRed: delivery.creds: the hosted arm resolves the SAME key and migrates NOTHING
mutations.cell: both compositions resolve ONE key - a host provisions from this string, so the flat kind writes where no daemon reads
